title: Recurrent cortical networks encode natural sensory statistics via sequence filtering
goal: Reproduce the original cortical sequence-order dependence and matched-versus-unmatched visual-context modulation using source-defined experiments, stimulation and cell selections, and indispensable controls.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: Original Figure 2 sequence-order population contrasts and required middle-pattern, nonstimulated-cell, single-pattern and spatial companions; original Figure 3 matched/unmatched incremental optogenetic responses relative to corresponding visual baselines, with opto-only comparisons across source experiments. Resolve final-paper/release identities; no automatic whole-paper or Figure5 mechanism requirement.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: simulation_method: RNN full32 prescribed-output loss and complete paired response curves remain a separate source-model demonstration. Preserve null rows, exact readout/time/reduction definitions and unresolved source-recipe differences; they do not reproduce empirical animal/context findings.
partial_empirical_support: Preserve existing Figure2C reconstruction and empirical notebook outputs as partial support; they do not establish the complete original empirical panel.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
Use an explicitly bound reproduction proposal only within its declared eligibility, comparison and execution limits; copying published findings is insufficient.

The preserved improvement.v1.json retains its declared comparison and coverage. Use retained_secondary_scope for its relationship to the corrected primary findings; satisfying a secondary or partial-component criterion alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement.

The primary same-target outcome bundle is unavailable. Any primary improvement requires an independently justified source-grounded comparison; no replacement metric, direction or tolerance is invented.
Keep the paper+data and paper+data+author-code outcomes separate. All scientific outcomes remain unknown until qualifying original-data execution and independent verification.
Preserve prior task definitions, improvement criteria and useful secondary implementations with their original scopes. Historical attempts and source metadata do not become qualified AI results.
